name: 0.20mm Speed @Northworks600x
notes: Speed-tuned variant of '0.20mm Standard'. Changes vs the vendor-derived baseline: outer wall 12.5->40 mm/s (their 15%-of-default was extraordinarily conservative), travel 133->250 mm/s (firmware allows ~316), accelerations 1000->1500 (emitted as M204 S, which raises the firmware value at RUNTIME - the config default stays 1000). First layer is deliberately left slow: the bed mesh spans ~2mm. NOT yet validated on the machine - see the notes in the vault before trusting it. ACCELERATION: left at 0 (not emitted). OrcaSlicer 2.4.2 was measured to honour only outer_wall_acceleration and travel_acceleration here - inner wall, infill and top surface emitted a fixed 1000 regardless of the configured value, giving an inconsistent scheme. Letting the firmware's own 'acceleration' govern uniformly is both correct and effective: raise it on the machine with 'M204 S1500' then 'M500'. TRAVEL SPEED: capped at 150 mm/s deliberately. CoreXY drives one motor at v*sqrt(2) on a 45-degree move, and the firmware's per-actuator ceiling is 316.7 mm/s (alpha/beta_max_rate 19000 mm/min) - so any travel above 224 mm/s overruns a motor on diagonals. An earlier 250 mm/s setting caused a real print failure: cumulative diagonal layer shift. Raise only after testing, and never above 224.
